subject: early-numeracy
title: Counting from 1 to 5
summary: Say 1 to 5 in order and count small groups of real things.

lesson.text: For a parent, older brother or sister, or anyone helping a young child: read this together and use things you already have at home.
Say the numbers slowly with the child: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Then let the child say them back to you.
Hold up one finger for 1, two fingers for 2, and keep going until all five fingers on one hand are up.
Put a few groundnuts, bottle tops or stones in a line. Touch each one as you say a number. Every thing gets one number only, and the last number you say tells you how many there are.

lesson.title: Counting cups
steps: Touch the first cup and say "one", the next "two", the last "three".
Ask: how many cups? The answer is the last number: three.

lesson.text: Children remember numbers better with songs. Count steps as you climb, count claps, and count the plates as you set them for dinner.
If the child skips a thing or counts one twice, don't scold. Count together again, slowly, touching each one.

questions.explanation: We count 1, 2, 3. So 3 comes after 2. 1 comes before 2, not after.

questions.prompt: Count the balls: ● ● ● ●. How many balls are there?
questions.explanation: Touch each ball and count: one, two, three, four. The last number is 4, so there are 4 balls.

questions.prompt: How many fingers are on one hand?
questions.explanation: Count them: thumb is one, then two, three, four, five. One hand has 5 fingers. 10 is the fingers on both hands.
We count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The number just before 5 is 4.
